paragraphs.title: Opening of the Prophecy and the Proclamation of Universal Destruction

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that the word of the LORD came unto Zephaniah.
easy.q: To whom did the word of the LORD come?

easy.explanation: The prophecy came in the days of Josiah, king of Judah.
easy.q: During whose reign was this prophecy given?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will utterly consume all things from off the land.”
easy.q: What did the LORD say He would consume from off the land?

medium.explanation: Verse 3 lists man, beast, the fowls of heaven, and the fishes of the sea.
medium.q: Which groups are specifically mentioned as being consumed?

answers: Things associated with sin and the wicked
medium.explanation: The stumblingblocks are mentioned together with the wicked as objects of judgment.
medium.q: What does “stumblingblocks” refer to in this passage?

answers: It cancels the statement in verse 2
It changes the subject to Josiah
medium.explanation: Verse 3 expands on the universal scope of the LORD’s judgment.
medium.q: How does verse 3 relate to the statement in verse 2?

answers: The judgment is limited to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The broad list emphasizes the sweeping extent of the announced destruction.
challenge.q: What does the list of people, animals, birds, and fish emphasize?

answers: His ancestry and his ministry during Josiah’s reign
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 gives Zephaniah’s ancestry and places the prophecy in Josiah’s days.
challenge.q: Which detail identifies both Zephaniah and the time of his prophecy?

challenge.explanation: The repetition stresses that the destruction will be extensive and complete.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated wording “I will consume”?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Idolatry and Abandonment of the Lord

answers: Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Verse 4 names Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
easy.q: Upon whom would the LORD stretch out His hand?

easy.explanation: The LORD said He would cut off the remnant of Baal.
easy.q: What would be cut off from the place?

answers: Those turned back from the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 6 mentions those turned back from the LORD and those who had not sought Him.
easy.q: Who had not sought the LORD?

answers: Those who worshipped on the housetops
medium.explanation: Verse 5 describes those who worshipped the host of heaven upon the housetops.
medium.q: Who worshipped the host of heaven?

answers: They abandoned or departed from Him
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who had turned away from the LORD.
medium.q: What does “turned back from the LORD” mean?

answers: They are all acts of obedience
They are all forms of service in the temple
medium.explanation: All three are included among the sinful practices subject to judgment.
medium.q: What do Baal worship, worship of the heavenly host, and turning from the LORD have in common?

answers: Swearing by the LORD and by Malcham
challenge.explanation: The passage condemns those who swear by the LORD and also by Malcham.
challenge.q: Which behavior shows divided religious allegiance?

answers: The first group combines loyalties, while the second abandons the LORD
The first group builds houses, while the second plants vineyards
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: One group mixes worship of the LORD with another allegiance; the other turns away from Him.
challenge.q: What is the difference between those who swear and those who turn back?

answers: They are connected with the condemned religious system
challenge.explanation: The Chemarims and priests are named in connection with the removal of Baal worship.
challenge.q: Why are the Chemarims mentioned with the priests?

paragraphs.title: The Day of the Lord and the Sins of the Ruling Classes

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “the day of the LORD is at hand.”
easy.q: What is said about the day of the LORD?

answers: The princes and the king’s children
easy.explanation: Verse 8 specifically names the princes and the king’s children.
easy.q: Whom would the LORD punish on the day of the sacrifice?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says they filled their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.
easy.q: With what did some people fill their masters’ houses?

answers: It is a prepared event of judgment
It is a joyful feast for everyone
medium.explanation: The LORD has prepared a sacrifice and invited guests, portraying a solemn judgment.
medium.q: What does the image of a sacrifice communicate about the day of the LORD?

answers: Foreign or unusual clothing associated with outside influence
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to clothing that reflects foreign or alien influence.
medium.q: What does “strange apparel” mean in context?

answers: They represent influential people and foreign practices under judgment
medium.explanation: The list includes ruling figures and people associated with foreign customs.
medium.q: Why are princes, the king’s children, and those in strange apparel mentioned together?

challenge.explanation: Their conduct is characterized by violence and deceit.
challenge.q: What moral quality is attributed to those who fill their masters’ houses?

answers: It emphasizes reverence and the seriousness of the coming judgment
It signals that the prophecy is finished
challenge.explanation: Silence before the Lord conveys awe because His day is near and solemn.
challenge.q: Why is the command “Hold thy peace” appropriate before the description of the day of the LORD?

answers: The day is at hand, and the LORD has prepared a sacrifice
The city will be rebuilt, and the people will prosper
The king has won a battle
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 first announces the nearness of the day and the prepared sacrifice.
challenge.q: Which details are given before the people who will be punished are listed?

paragraphs.title: Jerusalem’s Cry and Punishment for Wealth and Indifference

easy.explanation: Verse 10 mentions a cry from the fish gate.
easy.q: From which gate would a cry be heard?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh.”

answers: They would build and plant but not enjoy them
They would sell them to the king
They would enjoy them for many years
easy.explanation: They would build houses without inhabiting them and plant vineyards without drinking the wine.
easy.q: What would happen to the houses and vineyards of the people?

answers: A cry, a howling, and a great crashing
medium.explanation: The passage describes different sounds of distress from these places.
medium.q: What is heard from the fish gate, the second, and the hills?

answers: People complacent in their settled condition
medium.explanation: The expression describes people who are complacent and undisturbed in their security.
medium.q: What does “settled on their lees” describe?

answers: To examine even those hidden in complacency
medium.explanation: Searching with candles pictures a thorough investigation of the people.
medium.q: Why does the LORD search Jerusalem with candles?

answers: The belief that the LORD will not intervene at all
The belief that the LORD will save everyone
challenge.explanation: The complacent people wrongly believed that God would take no action.
challenge.q: What belief is expressed by the words, “The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil”?

answers: Those trusting in their possessions will lose them despite their complacency
Wealth is presented as a path to repentance
challenge.explanation: The passage condemns complacency and announces that possessions will become a booty.
challenge.q: How are wealth and indifference connected in this passage?

answers: Their plans will fail before they can benefit from them
They will move to another city
challenge.explanation: They will build and plant, but judgment will prevent them from enjoying the results.
challenge.q: What does the failure to enjoy houses and vineyards show about the sinners’ plans?

paragraphs.title: The Description of the Great and Unavoidable Day of the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 14 says the day is near and hastens greatly.
easy.q: How is the great day of the LORD described?

answers: The voice of the day, the trumpet, and the alarm
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the voice of the day, the trumpet, and the alarm.
easy.q: Which sounds are associated with the day of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says neither silver nor gold would be able to deliver them.
easy.q: What would not be able to deliver people?

answers: Wrath, trouble, distress, darkness, and gloominess
medium.explanation: Verse 15 lists wrath, trouble, distress, darkness, and gloominess.
medium.q: Which descriptions present the day as one of suffering and darkness?

answers: They will move without direction or understanding
medium.explanation: The image describes confusion and helplessness under judgment.
medium.q: What does “walk like blind men” mean in this context?

answers: Because they have sinned against the LORD
medium.explanation: Verse 17 directly connects their blindness-like wandering with their sin.
medium.q: Why will people walk like blind men?

answers: It shows that judgment is imminent and cannot be postponed
It shows that the day has already passed
It identifies a time of celebration
challenge.explanation: “Near” and “hasteth greatly” stress the urgency and certainty of judgment.
challenge.q: Why is the repeated emphasis on the nearness and speed of the day important?

answers: Even the strong will be unable to escape the day of the LORD
challenge.explanation: Even the mighty man will cry bitterly, showing that strength cannot prevent judgment.
challenge.q: What does the mighty man’s cry show?

answers: The fire represents consuming judgment, and wealth cannot deliver anyone
Silver and gold will feed the fire and save the people
The fire represents peace, and wealth represents restoration
challenge.explanation: The land will be devoured by the fire of the LORD’s jealousy, while silver and gold cannot rescue the people.
challenge.q: How do the fire, silver, and gold contribute to the passage’s conclusion?
